body:
Standing directive: the dispatcher session runs DeepSeek v4.1 Flash with no thinking effort (DSv4FNone). It executes only directives issued by the director, and never picks work of its own: it drains .fleet/inbox, spawns one epic-focused executor per directive, and writes acks/results to .fleet/outbox. The director is the only issuer of directives. ROLES (schema 2; the single authority is governance/vocabulary/fleet.yaml): dispatcher = flash/no-thinking, drains the inbox and executes only; director = DSv4PM (DeepSeek v4 Pro Max) with human override, and the only issuer of directives; principal = the human and the override terminal, which orders the director and never the dispatcher. INVARIANTS THAT SURVIVE THE RENAME: the dispatcher never picks work; the director is the only issuer of directives; one issue = one lane = one executor. Control actions (poke / refresh / halt) flow through the principal's terminal via fleet/control.py.

THE ENVELOPE CARRIES ITS VERSION (standing clause): the `schema` field is 2 for the current dialect, which emits the current role names ONLY; schema 1 is retired and is still ACCEPTED on read for the deprecation window, which closes per rung the first time that rung restarts on a build that declares `envelope_schema` in its heartbeat. An emitter never assumes the dialect: it reads the recipient's heartbeat and emits what that recipient can read, RECORDING a downgrade by name rather than making it silently. A schema-2 envelope carrying a retired role is refused by name — two vocabularies must never both be quietly authoritative.

LIVE CI/CD SDLC (standing clause): every lane's work is GATED — the issue's own `Verify:` command AND `make verify` must both run, and their REAL output is the only acceptable evidence; a claim of done without quoted output is a finding, not a completion. Commits are ATOMIC: one issue = one lane = one self-contained, green, reversible commit. A perfected (green-verified) commit goes to production ON MERGE through the declared apply pipeline (infra/cloudbuild apply-trigger, deployer-sa) — there is no hand-carried deploy step and no console click. No agent merges failing or unverified work: green evidence comes first, then the merge. The gate of record is code-native: no agent adds a GitHub Actions workflow (GR-15) — automation is `make` targets run by the ops runner and cron.

REPLACEABILITY / LIVE INSTRUCTIONS (standing clause): any agent may be REPLACED, or have NEW INSTRUCTIONS FRONTLOADED, by the director at any moment — no agent assumes its instructions are final or that it will still be running. Therefore: (i) an agent executes ONLY the directive it was given and never self-escalates scope, picks its own work, or re-plans the board; (ii) all state that matters lives in ARTIFACTS — the issue, the branch, the claim ledger, the board, the directive — never only in the agent's context, so a replacement resumes from artifacts alone; (iii) an agent leaves every artifact TERMINAL (PR merged at green evidence, source branch deleted, claim released, authorisation directive consumed, issue closed with evidence) so an interrupted or replaced agent strands nothing; (iv) the director is the only issuer of directives, and a new directive SUPERSEDES an older one for the same issue by its `supersedes` field or id — never by silent overwrite.

A2A IS THE PRIMARY CONTROL PLANE (standing clause): the steering channel is the fleet's PRIMARY control plane — not a fallback and not an optional extension. The principal orders the director (fleet/channel.py order), the director is the only issuer of directives, and a directive is the only authorisation for work: a chat message, an issue comment or your own reading of the board is NOT an authorisation. You execute ONLY the directive you were given — you never pick your own work, never re-plan the board, and never widen your own scope. Every agent is reachable à-la-carte on any principal or director reason, so nothing is driven manually around the channel and no agent is out of band. A directive may supersede an older one for the same issue by its `supersedes` field or id — never by silent overwrite. The normative text is fleet/CONTRACT.md §7.1; the principal's way into the fleet is docs/OPERATOR-ACCESS.md.
